title: Microprobe sampler and CI hooks for live-hotpath sampling
content:
Purpose
This doc describes the lightweight 'microprobe' sampler we started prototyping to collect short, periodic hotpath samples from inference servers and wire them into Perf CI jobs and nightly suites. Goal is: get actionable flamegraphs from production-like traffic without heavy continuous profiling or large storage burden.

Why micro-sampling?
- Low overhead: sub-1% CPU/latency impact when configured conservatively.
- Short windows (5s-60s) capture representative hotpaths during steady-state traffic.
- Easy to run inside CI, can be added to perf/regression tests as a post-run step.
- Works for both CPU and CUDA/GPU backends (using different samplers).

Components
1) microprobe-daemon (bash/python wrapper): triggers perf or bpftrace sampling for N seconds, uploads compressed stack samples to artifact storage.
2) sample-to-flame (node/python script): converts perf.data / bpftrace output into folded stacks and calls FlameGraph tool to render an SVG and a collapsed stacks text file.
3) ci-hook job: CI YAML snippet that runs microprobe during a short load generator run and attaches artifacts to the job.
4) quick-check scripts: local helpers to run on a dev machine or staging box.

Quickstart (CPU)
- install: apt-get install linux-tools-common linux-tools-$(uname -r) && git clone https://github.com/brendangregg/FlameGraph.git
- run a 10s sample: sudo ./microprobe-daemon --mode perf --pid $(pgrep -f redwood-server) --duration 10 --output /tmp/microprobe-$(date +%s).tar.gz
- generated artifact contains: perf.data, folded.txt, flame.svg, meta.txt

microprobe-daemon behaviour (high level)
- validates kernel has PERF_SAMPLE_STACK and frame pointers enabled (falls back to bpftrace minimal stacks if not).
- chooses event (cycles, cpu-clock) based on mode.
- optionally uses perf record -g --call-graph dwarf for C++ stacks; on very short samples, use -F 4000 to increase sample density.

BPFTrace fallback (for frame-pointer-less kernels)
- simple example to record user-space ustack: sudo bpftrace -e 'uretprobe:/usr/bin/redwood-server:0x*: @{ustack();}' -::: this is illustrative; our microprobe uses a compact bpftrace script that aggregates folded stacks and emits counts every second.

GPU sampling notes (NVIDIA)
- NVPROF is deprecated; prefer nsight-systems (nsys) or CUPTI-based sampling. For short live samples we use nsys CLI:
  nsys profile --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --sampling=cpu --output=/tmp/nsys-$(date +%s) --duration=8 --trace=cuda,osrt ./redwood-server-binary
- for kernel-level GPU stacks we rely on CUPTI-based stack collection and post-process with nsys or convert to collapsed stacks.
- caution: sampling GPUs in multi-tenant GPU nodes can interfere with other processes—use isolated test nodes.

CI job snippet (GitLab/Circle/GHA; generic YAML)
- stage: perf
  job: microprobe-smoke
  image: ubuntu:22.04
  script:
    - ./ci/setup-serving-runtime.sh
    - ./ci/start-stubload.sh --concurrency 8 --duration 30s &
    - sleep 5
    - sudo ./tools/microprobe-daemon --mode perf --pid $(pgrep -f redwood-server) --duration 15 --output artifacts/microprobe.tar.gz
    - ./tools/sample-to-flame artifacts/microprobe.tar.gz artifacts/flame.svg
  artifacts:
    paths: [artifacts/microprobe.tar.gz, artifacts/flame.svg]
  when: on_success

Interpreting results
- Open flame.svg in the CI job UI to spot hot functions. Look for tall, wide frames (consumers of CPU/host time).
- Compare folded.txt across runs using diff or our lightweight stack-compare script: it prints top-N delta by sample counts. Use this in perf regression alerts.

Regression detection heuristics (proposed)
- baseline-collection: nightly run collects 3 micro-samples at low load and stores collapsed stacks and top-20 list.
- alert if a function's relative sample share increases by >25% and absolute increase >= 50 samples across two consecutive nights.
- flag changes where tail latency correlation exists (combine trace-level p50/p95 with sample spikes).

Troubleshooting tips
- Too few samples: increase duration or frequency (-F for perf). If CI environment has short-lived processes, target parent pid and sample child processes too.
- Missing symbols: install debug symbols for the runtime binary or use addr2line on addresses collected in perf.data.
- No GPU stacks: ensure CUPTI is installed and that the process was launched with NVTX markers if using nsight.
- High overhead: reduce sampling frequency or shorten window, use bpftrace aggregated counters instead of full stacks.

Open items / TODOs
- Add automatic mapping from collapsed stacks to source file/line via addr2line + stored build-ids (requires debug-symbol artifact storage).
- Integrate with Optimize: produce recommended batching/kv-cache changes when specific hot functions correlate with dispatcher hot loops.
- Add an option to fuzz load profiles during sampling to make hotpaths more representative.
- Investigate eBPF offload to collect stack traces with less overhead for high-concurrency workloads.

Appendix: useful one-liners
- Generate folded stacks from perf: sudo perf script | ./FlameGraph/stackcollapse-perf.pl > folded.txt
- Build flamegraph: ./FlameGraph/flamegraph.pl folded.txt > flame.svg
- Convert nsys report to collapsed stacks (work-in-progress): nsys export -t summary -o /tmp/nsys-summary.sqlite && ./tools/nsys-to-folded /tmp/nsys-summary.sqlite > folded-nsys.txt

Contacts
- owner: Aisha Patel (eng-serving-runtime)
- backup: Liam Chen

Notes
This is intentionally lightweight and experimental; the idea is to make short, reproducible sampling cheap so more engineers will run it locally and in CI. Keep this doc as a living runbook for patterns that actually find regressions in nightly perf CI.
